title: Totally True History (Mostly)
blurb: Presidents, landmarks, toys and candy. Every card has three facts, and one is cap.

cards.say: George Washington [had just one of his own teeth left when he became president], [lived in the White House during his last year as president], [became an official land surveyor when he was 17], and [got a donkey from the King of Spain and started raising mules].
cards.real: The White House wasn't finished until 1800, after Washington's presidency. John Adams was the first president to live there.

cards.say: Abraham Lincoln [got an award from the National Wrestling Hall of Fame], [was born on the very same day as Charles Darwin], [got a patent for a way to lift boats over sandbars], and [had his voice recorded, and you can still hear it today].
cards.real: No recording of Lincoln exists. He died 12 years before Thomas Edison invented the phonograph in 1877.

cards.say: Theodore Roosevelt [was the first president to fly in an airplane while in office], [had kids who kept a green snake named Emily Spinach], [was the first president to ride in a submarine], and [was the first American to win a Nobel Prize].
cards.real: His first airplane ride was in 1910, the year after he left office. Franklin Roosevelt was the first to fly while president.

cards.say: Mount Rushmore [was meant to show the presidents down to their waists], [has a hidden tunnel cut 70 feet into the rock behind the heads], [took 41 years to carve, from start to finish], and [had Jefferson's face blasted off and carved again on Washington's other side].
cards.real: Carving started in October 1927 and ended in October 1941, so it took 14 years.

cards.say: The White House [was first painted white to hide burn marks from a fire in 1814], [got its official name from Theodore Roosevelt in 1901], [had a flock of sheep trim its lawn during World War I], and [has 132 rooms, and 35 of them are bathrooms].
cards.real: It was whitewashed when it was first built, to protect the stone, long before 1814. The burn-mark story is a myth.

cards.say: The Liberty Bell [cracked the first time it was rung in Philadelphia], [got its famous name during the American Revolution], [has Pennsylvania spelled with a missing N on it], and [was hidden under a church floor to keep it from the British].
cards.real: It got the name Liberty Bell in the 1830s, from people working to end slavery.

cards.say: Chocolate [is made from beans the ancient Maya used as money], [was worth so much that people made fake cacao beans from clay], [got its first factory-made candy bars in England in 1847], and [comes from a tree that first grew wild in Africa].
cards.real: Cacao trees come from the rainforests of South America. The first people known to use cacao lived in what's now Ecuador.

cards.say: Dr. Seuss [had Seuss as his real middle name, not his last name], [wrote Green Eggs and Ham using just 50 different words], [had a license plate on his car that said GRINCH], and [trained to be a medical doctor before he wrote books].
cards.real: He never studied medicine. He added Dr. to his name partly for his dad, who had hoped he would become a doctor.

cards.say: Mickey Mouse [was voiced by Walt Disney himself for almost 20 years], [was the first cartoon character with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame], [made his first appearance in a full-color cartoon], and [starred in two cartoons that were made before his first one came out].
cards.real: His first cartoon, Steamboat Willie in 1928, was black and white. His cartoons didn't switch to color until The Band Concert in 1935.

cards.say: Mr. Potato Head [got 44 votes in a race for mayor in Idaho], [was the first toy ever advertised on TV], [started out with parts you stuck into a real potato], and [didn't get a plastic potato body until 1964].
cards.real: He got just four votes in the 1985 race for mayor of Boise, Idaho.

cards.say: The Slinky [was invented by a naval engineer after a spring fell off a shelf], [was first sold at a store in New York City], [got its name from a word the inventor's wife found in a dictionary], and [was used by soldiers in the Vietnam War as a radio antenna].
cards.real: It was first sold at Gimbels in Philadelphia in 1945, where all 400 sold out in 90 minutes.

cards.say: Crayola crayons [came in a box of eight for a nickel in 1903], [got their name from the wife of one of the company's owners], [had a sharpener built into the very first box], and [came from a company that made red coloring for barn paint].
cards.real: The built-in sharpener came in 1958, with the first 64-color box. The first box, in 1903, had just eight crayons.
